gap: No family in this registry reads 410(a)'s base definition of employment. Within the United States, service is employment "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either" (clause (A)(i)). Outside the United States, 410(a) makes service employment only (A)(ii) on or in connection with an American vessel or American aircraft under a contract of service entered into within the United States, or one during which the craft touches at a United States port, while the employee is employed on and in connection with it, "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either"; (B) "by a citizen or resident of the United States" (before 1984, "a citizen of the United States": Pub. L. 98-21 section 323(a)(2), for remuneration paid after 1983) as an employee (i) of an American employer or (ii) of a foreign affiliate of an American employer "during any period for which there is in effect an agreement, entered into pursuant to section 3121(l)" with respect to the affiliate (Pub. L. 98-21 section 321(b), for agreements entered into after April 20, 1983, or for an earlier agreement whose American employer elects the amendment under section 321(f), wrote "American employer" for "a domestic corporation" and "affiliate" for "subsidiary"); or (C) "regardless of where or by whom performed", where an agreement under section 433 designates the service as employment or recognizes it as equivalent to employment (added by Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(a)(1), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983). So a case or residual that reads covered does not reach service outside the United States that none of (A)(ii), (B) and (C) reaches: a noncitizen's before 1984, and a nonresident noncitizen's from 1984, that is not on or in connection with an American vessel or aircraft as (A)(ii) states and that no section 433 agreement designates; and a citizen's or resident's service abroad for an employer that is neither an American employer nor a foreign affiliate under a 3121(l) agreement in effect, unless a section 433 agreement designates it. That holds for a Federal employer as for any other: POMS RS 01901.340 A names "services performed outside the U.S. by an alien" as excluded by some other provision of law (review r6 M-5, r7 H-2 and low 9).
